Actual behavior read from games/gs1/asm/080788c4.s: entry = inv->inventory[slot]; if entry==0 return -1; else if ((entry & 0xf800) != 0) decrement the top 5-bit count field by one unit (entry -= 0x800) and return 1; else clear the slot, compact all non-zero 16-bit entries in inventory[0..14] to the front (in a descending 15-iteration loop with separate read/write raw pointers), zero-fill the remaining tail entries computed fresh from the saved base pointer (base+count), return 2. Always calls Func_08077428(owner) before returning.

Iterated 6 candidate respellings, converging from wrong_instructions=78 (candidate 140B) down to wrong_instructions=50 (candidate 128B, reference 132B). Fixes that measurably helped: (a) not pre-materializing the OwnerState_Get() pointer into a dedicated named local before its first struct-field use -- this alone dropped an extra push{r8}/mov r8,r0 that the reference does not have (reference keeps the pointer live in r0 across the whole first branch, never spilling it to a callee-saved register until the loop-counter reuse forces it into r6); (b) reusing the (entry & 0xf800) intermediate value (named `masked`) for the inv->inventory[slot]=0 store on the else path, matching reference's reuse of the ANDS result register instead of loading a fresh literal 0; (c) computing the zero-fill destination as a fresh `base + count` expression (a separate `fill` pointer) rather than continuing the compaction loop's `dst` pointer, matching reference's fresh 'lsls r3,r5,#1; adds r0,r3,r6' recompute from the saved base register.

Residual gap after these fixes: a small, completely systematic register swap persists for the whole first branch -- the initial ldrh destination and the (entry & 0xf800) computation land in r2/r3 in the candidate versus r3/r2 in the reference (every instruction in that stretch is a same-opcode, same-operands-modulo-r2<->r3 swap). Tried both `entry & 0xf800` and `0xf800 & entry` operand order, tried a chained `entry = (inv = OwnerState_Get(owner))->inventory[slot];` versus two plain statements, and tried moving `s32 result = -1;` before/after the OwnerState_Get call -- none of these changed which scratch register the compiler picked for the ldrh result, so this is not one of the source-shape levers I have visibility into.

Second residual gap: the `base = inv->inventory;` (struct-offset-216 pointer materialization) compiles as 'adds r0,#216 (in place); adds r4,r0,#0 (copy)' in the candidate but as 'adds r6,r0,#0 (copy first); adds r6,#216 (in place on the copy)' in the reference -- same two Thumb instructions (ADDS Rd,#imm8 requires Rd==Rn so a copy+in-place-add is unavoidable for a >7 immediate), just the copy-vs-add-first ordering and destination register number differ. This looks like a genuine compiler-internals residual (which physical register the allocator hands to a freshly-declared local that happens to be exactly a dead-source's value) rather than something a further source respelling can steer, so it is flagged for permuter-style search rather than more manual guessing.

Did not attempt further permutations beyond these six; the remaining diff is concentrated in these two systematic, non-semantic register-choice differences rather than any remaining logic/shape mismatch, so a permuter targeting register-allocation order (not control flow) is the most promising next step.
